svg.title: Container runtime stack: containerd, runc and OCI
svg.desc: Docker (when you type docker run) and Kubernetes both hand the job to containerd. 1: containerd, the Manager, tracks every container on the machine, fetches images, sets up networking, starts and stops containers; a floor manager. 2: runc, the Worker, builds one container with namespaces and cgroups, starts the app, then steps away; a builder. Result: your container is running. On the side, OCI, the Rulebook, is not a program but a set of standards (image spec and runtime spec) that containerd and runc follow: the one box size agreed in 2015, like a building code. Remember: Manager, Worker, Rulebook. Kubernetes manages many machines; containerd manages containers on one machine.

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
text.tspan: Who actually runs a container? The Manager, the Worker and the Rulebook

text.tspan: You never type these yourself: Docker and Kubernetes talk to them for you
